primary_unique_math_proof: In coordinates relative to gap center, stationary contact corners are(-1/2,1) and(1/2,1). A unit square at45 degrees has halfdiagonal r=sqrt2/2.
Let its bottom vertex height be b. Its lower-left edge is y=b-x, so actual contact(-1/2,1) implies b=1/2. Its top vertex is a full diagonal sqrt2 above bottom:height(B)=1/2+sqrt2, uniquely D.
For b>1/2 there is a gap and for b<1/2 the corner penetrates the diamond, so first contact uniquely fixes b. The unit side has vertical projection sqrt2/2, and is not the entire vertical diagonal.

The physical square can carry the two blue side styles under the actual rotation: the original right side maps exactly to the selected lower-right side. Red points identify stationary contacts only. Thus unlike the Plane242 counter-reading, no competing ink-preservation picture choice is created.
